pattern.top_pattern: Smaller acute hospital pockets are emerging in CA, IN, and NY
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA / IN / NY acute hospital spend in DSNP HMO and Medicare HMO
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: Several smaller acute hospital pockets are emerging outside the main TX and VA markets, with recurring signals in CA, IN, and NY. These are low-volume patterns, but they show meaningful paid-per-admit increases and repeated kidney and urinary DRGs. Treat them as early-warning pockets that need targeted review before they scale into broader spend issues.
pattern.why_it_matters: Small-volume hospital pockets can become material quickly if they are not checked while they are still concentrated and actionable.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run targeted case and payment review on LOS ANGELES MEDICAL CENTER and the named kidney and urinary DRGs in CA, IN, and NY to determine whether these are isolated events or the start of repeatable provider patterns.
evidence_summary: CA / IN DSNP HMO acute hospital pressure and smaller CA / NY Medicare HMO pockets total about +$570K.
LOS ANGELES MEDICAL CENTER added about +$128K across CA DSNP HMO PA categories, with one non-PA pocket showing paid per admit up about $8.5K.
IN kidney and urinary DRGs under DSNP HMO added about +$264K combined, and NY Medicare HMO Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC added +$115K.
